hints.title: Problem Analysis
hints.text: We want user IDs who hold at least one 'Refinance' and at least one 'Mortgage' loan.

hints.title: Algorithmic Strategy
hints.text: Use conditional counts or sum(loan_type = '...') in the having clause to verify presence of both types.

hints.title: Implementation
hints.text:
```sql
SELECT user_id 
FROM Loans 
GROUP BY user_id 
HAVING SUM(loan_type = 'Refinance') > 0 
   AND SUM(loan_type = 'Mortgage') > 0 
ORDER BY user_id ASC;
```

variables: N: total records in primary table
complexity.notes: Efficient execution matching optimal computational complexity.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Brute force exceeds standard time constraints.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Identify core invariants and leverage optimal structures.

solutions.code:
SELECT user_id 
FROM Loans 
GROUP BY user_id 
HAVING SUM(loan_type = 'Refinance') > 0 
   AND SUM(loan_type = 'Mortgage') > 0 
ORDER BY user_id ASC;

SELECT user_id 
FROM Loans 
GROUP BY user_id 
HAVING COUNT(CASE WHEN loan_type = 'Refinance' THEN 1 END) > 0 
   AND COUNT(CASE WHEN loan_type = 'Mortgage' THEN 1 END) > 0 
ORDER BY user_id ASC;
